newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - German shares hit new record, franc falters.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German shares hit new record, franc falters.

text.p: German shares stormed to a new record close on Thursday and French stocks also surged after comments by a Bank of France policymaker pushed the dollar higher against the franc and the mark.
Bank of France monetary policy council member Jean-Pierre Gerard said in an interview with Le Monde he wanted a stronger dollar against the mark, implying a desire for a weaker franc.
One way to get the dollar higher would be to cut short-term rates in France and Germany, making equities more attractive.

"Unfortunately we have little influence on German monetary policy," he was quoted as saying. "A second possibility, given that we cannot get a concerted reduction in rates, would be to modify the franc-mark parity."

Analysts said the French government needs a higher dollar/mark rate to resolve economic problems highlighted in the domestic debate about foreign exchange policy but it also needs the collusion of the Bundesbank to achieve it.

"Gerard is very much on the dovish extreme on the Bank of France but there's no doubt the steady stream of these comments does create creeping suspicions about franc fort," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at Bank of America.
Critics of French exchange rate policy believe the dollar is undervalued against the German mark and the franc, slowing French growth and employment by giving U.S. exports an edge.
Around 1530 gmt, the franc stood at 3.3925 per mark having been as low as 3.3972 earlier and compared with 3.3860 late on Wednesday, and at 5.2007 against the dollar after 5.1725.

French shares were around 0.9 percent higher, having been slightly higher at midday. Prices rose smartly during the morning as the franc fell against the dollar boosting the outlook for French exporting companies.

Some traders were also betting there would be an early end to the French lorry drivers' strike, now in its 11th day, and there was a scramble to cover short positions in the futures market ahead of a contract expiry on Friday, traders said.
Germany's DAX index of 30 top shares ended bourse trade at a record closing high, after the dollar raced to its highest level for a month against the mark.
The DAX index closed at 2,817.49 points, up 0.73 percent, or 20.46 points, just below its all-time intraday record high of 2,819.95 points reached on Tuesday.
The dollar penetrated the 1.53 mark level, after Gerard's comments, particularly benefiting Germany's export-oriented chemicals and auto sectors.
But dealers said volumes were somewhat dampened due to the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States.
In after hours trading the DAX Ibis index was up more that one percent, or 33.65 points, at 2,825.32 points.
Shares in Europe's biggest carmaker Volkswagen AG continued to be at the centre of attention and recovered two percent, closing bourse dealings up 11.70 marks at 613 marks.
Sources close to the firm said production chief Jose Ignacio Lopez de Arriortua, at the centre of alleged industrial espionage charges, was set to offer his resignation on Friday.
In London declining drug stocks dragged FTSE-100 index lower as Wall Street's closure for the Thanksgiving Day holiday robbed the market of fresh direction.
Unsettled by yesterday's Dow decline and renewed fears of rising interest rates after Tuesday's British budget, the market was down around 0.2 percent.
Traders said the market was likely to be marooned near its current levels with Wall Street unlikely to see much action in tomorrow's post-holdiay session.

The dollar pushed higher against the yen in Europe and dealers said the reason was the Bank of Japan's uninspiring quarterly Tankan report of business confidence on Wednesday. "It is a carry-over from the tankan report, which was weaker than expected, and the belief that (Japanese) rates will not rise," said a senior dealer at a British bank.

In metals, Copper prices rose above $2,300 a tonne, the highest since the Sumitomo Corp scandal erupted in June, as critically low inventory levels forced buyers to scramble for metal, traders and analysts said.
During the morning gold was fixed at $372.20, its lowest fix in over 2-1/2 years, as soaring stock markets and the stronger dollar pulled investor money out of bullion.
CURRENCIES at 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.66 yen and 1.5327 marks against 113.33 yen and 1.5275 marks in late Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 9.0 points at 4,040.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 19.52 at 2,290.29.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 20.46 at 2817.49.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $372.65 up from $372.20 during the morning which was the lowest fix since April 25, 1994.
